clue: Bell Boulder arch with brass twig-bell

atlas.why: a fish close to camera beside a small brass bell above a stony bottom: the staging for the trout in the foreground of beat 3

takes.seen: 0-1 s cockpit matches the master (six-bolt port with chip at two o'clock, hinge and latch, empty ballast slot, chalk chart, lamp toggle, amber lamp, dent at right) with a dark arch shape in the port; about 0.7-2.5 s a turkey tail fan and blue head come in at lower right, the head at the toggle at about 1 s, and an amber beam comes on through the port by about 2 s; 2.5-5.6 s push-in to the glass, the mossy boulder arch with the brass bell on a twig and a knotted cord, a speckled trout under the bell facing right at about 4-5 s and then to the right of the bell facing left with its mouth open at about 5.6 s, Turkey's faint reflection lower left, beam from below as in the still; about 6.0 s a transition frame shows the tin, Turkey, the bell and the trout together inside a porthole rim; 6.6-8 s river side as the outside master: riveted tin with dent on the pebble bed, Turkey small behind the amber port, a knot of cord tied on the tin's top handle, two speckled trout at the left foreground facing the port

open: beat 3 loses the thing: from about 6.6 s there is no arch and no bell on Trout's side, only a knot of cord on the tin's handle, so 'polite ferry customer or bell-ringer prank' has nothing to point to except that knot; the bell over the tin is seen only in the transition frame at about 6.0 s
the cut is not hard: at about 6.0 s a morph frame shows the tin and Turkey inside a porthole rim with the bell and trout in front, and Turkey's reflection still at lower left
a turkey tail fan and head, not a wing tip, fill the lower right corner in beat 1 (about 0.7-3.5 s); the head or beak, not a wing, is at the lamp toggle
the clockwise circle (the row's rule) cannot be confirmed: the trout is seen below the bell facing right and then right of it facing left, with no full loop visible in the frames

the bell swinging and the cord being pulled are not readable in stills; the bell hangs nearly plumb in every frame, so 'tripwire alarm or dinner bell' rests on the trout stopping open-mouthed beside the cord at about 5.6 s; nothing arrives to eat and nothing reacts as to an alarm
two trout in beat 3 where one was asked for; neither is seen circling
the tin is not shown rocking and the cord is not seen running from the handle up to anything
sound was not checked (whether a bell is heard)
beat 2 adds little over the still: same composition, bell, cord, trout, reflection and beam, with a small move of the trout
